name_note: The genomes GTDB places in this species carry the NCBI names Clostridium phoceensis and Lawsonibacter asaccharolyticus; the sentences below cite work published under the latter name.

sentences.text: Lawsonibacter asaccharolyticus is an obligately anaerobic, Gram-positive, non-spore-forming rod first isolated from a faecal sample of a healthy Japanese woman.
It produces acetate and butyrate as metabolic end-products and belongs to a cluster with the genera Pseudoflavonifractor and Flavonifractor in the family Ruminococcaceae.
Its genome carries genes for butyrate synthesis.

A multi-cohort analysis of 22,867 participants with dietary information reported that the link between coffee consumption and the microbiome was largely driven by the presence and abundance of this species.
That study also reported that coffee can stimulate growth of L. asaccharolyticus in vitro.
